title: Random Walks on Critical FK–Ising Maps and Liouville Brownian Motion
main_claim: Start r random walks independently from the corner measure deg/(2n) on critical spherical FK-Ising maps with n edges, speed time up by exactly n, and use any deterministic metric scale a_n for which the maps converge in GHP to the sqrt3-LQG sphere. Then the maps together with the r walks converge jointly, in the curve-decorated GHP topology, to (S, D_h, mu_h) with r independent stationary Liouville Brownian motions, using the half-energy convention (1/2)∫|∇f|^2.
coverage:
Read all five sections in full and checked every proof step.
- Sec 2: graph-energy identity E_n(u,v) = 1/2 Σ d_e u d_e v, including the loop and multiplicity conventions. Consistency B_n = 2G_n with the unit-conductivity energy Σ(d_e w)^2 → ∫|∇χ|^2 and the half-energy LBM clock. Arctan-center lemma: shift identity, continuity, and the algebra for log(a_n/â_n).
- Sec 3: functional calculus J_n e^{-sG_n} J_n^* = Π + ψ_s(2K_n), including how it acts on constants and on the orthogonal complement of the discrete space. Resolvent analogue r_α(y) = αy/(1+αy). Fdd product formula. Resolvent graph convergence.
- Sec 4: clipping cutoff recovery (sign trick, support, buffer). Lyons–Zheng forward/backward identity, derived by hand. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz weights (1/2, 1/4, 1/4) and the Doob constants, which give exactly 2‖v‖² + 40T⟨v,Av⟩. Form-norm expansion and spectral dominated convergence. Bounds 0 ≤ u ≤ 1 and ‖G_n u‖ ≤ α. Separating cutoffs. Optional sampling with an F_τ-measurable index. Order of limits in the Aldous bound. Continuity of limits from vanishing jump size.
- Sec 5: ambient chain metric, including the non-shortening argument for c_n = δ_n/2 + a_n, the Hausdorff bounds and the Prokhorov bound. ρ→D_h transfer. Exponential-clock Doob bound 4⌊nT⌋/n². Cable interpolation distance and passage to C([0,∞)). Pointwise conditional convergence followed by bounded convergence over environments.
- Cross-checked that the cited companion results (SC Lemma 2.3, Prop 2.4, Lemma 5.1, Thm 5.2, Prop 8.3, Lemma 9.1) exist in the SC source with matching content. SC sections are input in the order 1-2-3-4-6-7-5-8-9, so SC's Theorem 5.2 is the unit-conductivity theorem.
- Not verified: the companion's proofs themselves (unit conductivity, Hilbert–Schmidt inverse convergence, geometric extraction). The sibling rank-42 review covers those partially.
sibling_notes: This paper is the path-level corollary of the Spectral-convergence companion (rank 42, no_gap_found, partial). All the substantial inputs come from there: common coordinate, unit conductivity Thm 5.2, centered-inverse HS convergence, and the closed continuum form Prop 8.3. Inside this paper, the passage from those inputs to time-parametrized quenched path convergence, using a stationary Lyons–Zheng bound plus Aldous, is self-contained and correct. Its soundness therefore reduces to the companion's.
